Cryptography on the RP2350: a matched Arm / RISC-V pair

Cortex-M33 and Hazard3 · seven libraries · classical and post-quantum · single and dual core · 18–558 MHz at 1.05 V and 1.60 V · sweep v2.6.7, shootout v2.6.3, baselines v2.4.0–v2.6.5 · one board (E0E14525E64AF6ED), September 2026

The six things worth remembering 1. At the default 150 MHz, post-quantum cryptography is a tie between the cores: ML-KEM and ML-DSA are within ±4%. Classical software still favours the M33: 1.5–2.2x for Monocypher, micro-ecc and RSA, 2.6x for p256-m, and 1.0–1.3x for Mbed TLS depending on the build.
2. Library choice still matters more than the core. micro-ecc signs P-256 1.4x faster than Mbed TLS on the M33, and Monocypher does X25519 9.5x faster than Mbed TLS.
3. Every suite except the M33 post-quantum pair passes 540–558 MHz on both cores at 1.60 V. The highest clock where everything passed on both is 351 MHz, because the M33 post-quantum suites locked up at 400 MHz and needed a manual power cycle.
4. Overclocking fails in four different ways: a hang the watchdog catches, a lockup it does not, core 1 stopping while core 0 carries on, and, once, a wrong ML-DSA-87 result on Hazard3 at 546 MHz. Ceilings move by up to 200 MHz between runs.
5. The toolchain moved Hazard3 more than the M33: GCC 16.1 made ML-DSA signing 16–22% cheaper but Mbed TLS ECDSA 16% more expensive.
6. ML-DSA signing cost depends on the input by up to 6.6x, so compare signing times only on the same key and message.

All runs execute from XIP flash. Libraries: Mbed TLS 3.6.6 (NIST_OPTIM, HAVE_ASM), p256-m, micro-ecc (Arm assembly without UMAAL; portable C on Hazard3), Monocypher, mlkem-native, mldsa-native (reduced-RAM), RP2350 SHA-256 and TRNG, Pico SDK 2.3.1. Sweeps validate every step byte-exact against references captured at 150 MHz, with a 6 s watchdog and a flash journal that resumes after a reset.

16. Caveats

SamplesTwo overclock runs per core, one board. Ceilings moved by up to 200 MHz between runs; treat them as observations, not ratings.
Beyond the datasheet1.60 V is outside the RP2350's rated range (1.30 V maximum). There was no thermal or supply telemetry: VSYS reads ADC full scale and the die temperature sensor is unusable on this board.
Silent corruptionHazard3's ML-DSA-87 result at 546 MHz was wrong without a hang or an error code, so a passing step does not prove the next one is merely slow.
Watchdog escapeFive M33 lockups needed a manual power cycle. An unattended device overclocked this far could stay locked up.
BuildsThe sweep (5c3273beb52e) and shootout (1edd0410f83b) are different source revisions and different binaries. Mbed TLS moves by up to 25% with flash layout, which is why its sweep and shootout ratios differ.
Timing resolutionTRNG reads take 5–6 µs at high clocks, so its ops/s figures are timer-quantised. Dual-core gains for slow ECC suites alternate between fixed values, including impossible values above 2.0.
Rejection samplingML-DSA signing is a single draw per level and input.
ConfigurationML-DSA is built reduced-RAM; the pairwise consistency self-tests are disabled in both post-quantum libraries. Side channels were not measured.
Measured on Raspberry Pi Pico 2 hardware, board E0E14525E64AF6ED, 19–24 September 2026. Stability is judged by byte-exact comparison of deterministic outputs against references captured at 150 MHz. Voltages above 1.30 V are outside the RP2350 datasheet operating range.
